title: Communicating in a federated learning environment

pse.problem: Inefficiencies and delays in federated learning due to variable response times among participants and potential drop-outs during training sessions.
pse.solution_function: In the federated learning environment, a monitoring operation identifies stragglers (late responders) or drop-outs (non-responders). The system assigns participants into tiers based on their factors, each tier having a designated wait time. The aggregator queries the selected tier and tracks response times of the participants. If a participant fails to respond within the designated wait time, they are either classified as stragglers or drop-outs depending on the embodiment. The training of the federated learning model is updated using collected replies from participating federated learning participants, along with computed predictions for the stragglers or drop-outs.
pse.solution_structure: The system comprises a plurality of federated learning participants, an aggregator, and possibly a communication module. The federated learning participants maintain local data sources and collaborate with the aggregator during training sessions.
pse.solution_implementation: During each round of updating the training of the federated learning model, the system monitors the response times of federated learning participants. If a number of run epochs is less than a number of synchronization epochs, responses are received and the response time is updated until a maximum time elapses. If a number of run epochs exceeds the number of synchronization epochs, federated learning participants are designated as drop-outs when their response time exceeds a predetermined threshold. In some embodiments, the system creates histograms of remaining response times or assigns average reply times to each tier.
pse.effect: The solution reduces delays and inefficiencies by efficiently managing communication between the aggregator and federated learning participants, minimizing impact from stragglers and drop-outs during federated learning training sessions.
